headline: BNP authorizes Tarique Rahman to finalize presidential candidate
summary: The party's Standing Committee has entrusted the BNP Chairman with the responsibility of nominating the candidate for the presidency.
details: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has officially authorized its Chairman, Tarique Rahman, to decide on the nomination of the party's presidential candidate.
The decision was made by the party's Standing Committee, granting the party chief the sole authority to finalize who will represent the BNP in the presidential race.
According to the Home Minister, the final decision regarding the candidate's identity will rest with Tarique Rahman.
This move centralizes the nomination process, placing the key strategic decision in the hands of the party's top leadership.
caption:
Who will be the BNP's presidential candidate? The decision now rests solely with Tarique Rahman.

The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has officially authorized its Chairman, Tarique Rahman, to decide on the nomination of the party's presidential candidate.

The decision was made by the party's Standing Committee, granting the party chief the sole authority to finalize who will represent the BNP in the presidential race.

According to the Home Minister, the final decision regarding the candidate's identity will rest with Tarique Rahman.

This move centralizes the nomination process, placing the key strategic decision in the hands of the party's top leadership.

#Bangladesh #BNP #TariqueRahman #Politics #PresidentialNomination

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Somoy News, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo

headline_marked: Police HQ issues [[nationwide highest alert over threat]] to vehicles
headline: Police HQ issues nationwide highest alert over threat to vehicles
summary: Security has been tightened across the country after intelligence reports suggested potential attacks on police jeeps, pickups, and buses.
details: Police Headquarters has issued a nationwide highest alert following threats of potential sabotage targeting police vehicles.
An emergency message sent from the Operations Control Room on Saturday, August 1, warned that extremist groups or miscreants could target police jeeps, pickups, and buses.
Intelligence agencies provided the information, prompting the Police HQ to order all field-level units to strengthen their security measures.
The headquarters described the matter as 'extremely important' and urged the strict implementation of the directives.
While officials have not made formal statements, some have claimed that such alerts are part of regular operational activities.
